One of the classic divers out there!✨ The Rolex Submariner Date is more than just one of the world’s most recognisable dive watches, it is the benchmark by which countless others are judged. Since its introduction in 1953, it has defined the modern dive watch, combining professional capability with timeless design in a way few watches have ever achieved. The current 41mm reference continues that legacy with subtle refinements that make an already iconic watch even better.

The black dial is a masterclass in legibility, with large Chromalight filled hour markers and the signature Mercedes hands delivering exceptional clarity in all conditions. Surrounding it is the black Cerachrom ceramic bezel, virtually scratch resistant and engineered for precise dive timing. The combination of the glossy black dial, ceramic bezel, and Oystersteel case creates a look that is instantly recognisable, equally at home beneath the waves or paired with everyday attire.

The 41mm Oystersteel case feels robust yet perfectly balanced on the wrist. Fitted with the Oyster bracelet, Oysterlock safety clasp, and Rolex’s ingenious Glidelock extension system, it offers exceptional comfort with effortless micro-adjustment, making it one of the finest bracelet and clasp combinations in the industry. With 300 metres of water resistance, the Submariner remains every bit the professional dive watch it was designed to be.

Powering the watch is Rolex’s in house Calibre 3235, a Superlative Chronometer movement featuring the blue Parachrom hairspring, Paraflex shock absorbers, and an impressive 70 hour power reserve. Combining outstanding reliability, precision, and durability, it perfectly complements a watch that has become one of the greatest icons in modern watchmaking, a true tool watch that continues to set the standard. 💫

A random photo resurfaced from my iPhone today, a snapshot of my collection taken before COVID.

Back then, F.P. Journe hadn’t yet become the darling of the collecting world because it wasn’t a Patek Philippe. Even the Richard Mille RM 67-02 barely turned heads, dismissed by many for being too thin and too small.

It’s fascinating how quickly the landscape changed. Hype took over. FOMO crept in. Suddenly, the very same watches became objects of obsession and the desirables of every heart. 

It serves as a reminder of something I’ve always believed: stay true to your own passion. The most interesting watches aren’t always the ones everyone is chasing. Sometimes, the greatest discoveries lie exactly where no one else is looking.

After all, isn’t that what collecting is really about? Isn’t the journey far more rewarding than simply arriving at the destination? Why are we falling into the traps of social media today?

The Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Hybris Artistica Calibre 179 is one of the most technically insane and artistically refined watches ever created in modern haute horology. Built around the Maison’s legendary multi-axis Gyrotourbillon, the watch combines extreme mechanical engineering with hand-finished artistic craftsmanship inside the iconic reversible Reverso case. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +2
At the heart of the watch is the fourth-generation Gyrotourbillon, composed of 123 components. The inner titanium cage rotates every 16 seconds, while the outer carriage completes a full rotation every minute, creating a floating anti-gravity effect visible from both dials. The flying construction makes the mechanism appear suspended in space beneath the sapphire crystal. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Powered by the hand-wound Calibre 179, the watch uses Jaeger-LeCoultre’s patented Duoface architecture, displaying two time zones across two completely different personalities. The front dial showcases geometric black lacquer artwork inspired by Art Deco architecture, while the reverse reveals a skeletonized mechanical universe surrounding the Gyrotourbillon. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
The craftsmanship is equally extraordinary. The pink or white gold bridges are laser-cut to create nearly 200 microscopic hollows, then individually hand-lacquered by a single artisan—an art mastered by only a few craftsmen inside the manufacture. Despite containing 382 components, the case remains only 13.63mm thick. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Limited to just 10 pieces worldwide, the watch reportedly carries a value around $600,000+, placing it among the rarest and most exclusive Reversos ever made. 
Collectors on Reddit described it as “the most beautiful timepiece” they had ever seen, while others compared the floating Gyrotourbillon to “sorcery on the wrist.”

When Piaget introduced the Polo in 1979, it challenged the conventions of luxury sports watches at their core. At a time when the category was increasingly defined by steel cases and overt technicality, Piaget chose a different path—one rooted in precious metal, fluid form, and lifestyle elegance. The original Polo was not conceived as a tool watch, but as a confident statement where case and bracelet merged into a single, continuous object

The defining feature of the Polo was its sequence of horizontal gadroons flowing uninterrupted across the case and integrated bracelet. Rather than separating functional elements, Piaget treated the watch as a sculptural whole. This philosophy aligned naturally with the maison’s long-standing expertise in gold craftsmanship and ultra-thin watchmaking, positioning the Polo as an expression of refinement and ease rather than performance-driven utility

The modern Polo 79 revisits this idea with remarkable fidelity, and the two-tone execution adds a subtle layer of historical resonance. By pairing white gold with polished yellow-gold gadroons, the watch recalls an era when bi-metal designs conveyed confidence without excess. The contrast is deliberate yet restrained: yellow gold highlights the Polo’s signature horizontal architecture, while white gold lends a cooler, contemporary balance

Powering the Two-Tone Polo 79 is Piaget’s ultra-thin automatic calibre 1200P. Built around a micro-rotor architecture, it preserves the watch’s slender profile while maintaining mechanical reliability. More importantly, the movement reflects Piaget’s belief that technical sophistication should serve design, not overshadow it. In the Polo 79, mechanics act as an enabler of elegance, reaffirming Piaget’s vision of luxury defined by harmony, precious materials, and effortless design.

The first VPC model to sell out was Type 37HW in Dove Grey.

We work in small batches of continuously evolving watches. This means that, once a batch is sold out, it is gone forever and moves to the VPC Archive on our website. This isn't intended as some false scarcity model or to trigger FOMO. Frankly, the watch market is far too cooled-off for that at the moment, so even if I wanted to, it wouldn't work. 

Instead, VPC is a creative endeavor for me. I have no interest in growing the company too much and pushing big numbers of watches. To me, the value lies in continuously dreaming up and developing truly special watches and executing them to an extremely high standard. This means each batch builds on the previous, evolving it in some small or large way. The fact that this makes each batch a little more special to the enthusiasts who own them is a great bonus. 

That's not to say I will never do anything like this again. Type 37HW will surely come back, but with different dials at the very least. In fact...I have a very small run of something exotic in the works. Subscribe to the newsletter on the website to be the first to know!

Some watches aim to impress through complications. Others prove that true refinement needs very little.

This Parmigiani Fleurier Tonda PF Micro-Rotor (ref. PFC914-1020023-100182) is a perfect example. Its Blue Agate dial, enhanced by the signature Grain d’Orge guilloché pattern, interacts beautifully with the light while remaining effortlessly understated. No date, no unnecessary distractions, just hours and minutes presented in their purest expression.

Turn the watch over, and the real masterpiece reveals itself: an in-house movement featuring a 950 platinum micro-rotor. This sophisticated architecture allows the watch to remain exceptionally slim while offering an unobstructed view of the movement, an elegant solution that is as technically demanding as it is visually captivating.

A watch that doesn’t seek attention, but quietly rewards those who take the time to truly appreciate it.

Claude André Genève was established in Geneva in 1982 by Sodimo SA, a company founded by entrepreneurs of Syrian origin. Built with Swiss craftsmanship but aimed primarily at the Levant, these watches found their home on wrists across Syria and its neighboring countries.

Then history intervened.

As the Syrian civil war unfolded, forgotten inventories began making their way into Turkey through Syrian dealers. Many arrived as genuine new old stock, untouched for decades, quietly preserved in warehouses while the world outside changed forever.

That is why a Claude André is more than a Swiss mechanical watch. It is a witness to trade, migration, resilience and the enduring ties between neighboring peoples. A reminder that even the smallest objects can carry stories far greater than themselves.

Sometimes, the most fascinating provenance is not written in a catalog.

It is written by history itself.

I'm asking: ✔️ What index is it tracking? ✔️ What's the expense ratio (MER if you're in Canada)? ✔️ What companies does it actually own? ✔️ Does it actually fit into my portfolio? content.description:
Omega Moonwatch Brothers 🧲🌘🚀

Saat dünyasının en büyük efsanelerinden biri olan Omega Speedmaster “Moonwatch”, horoloji tarihinin en ikonik kronografıdır. Onun hikayesi sadece laboratuvarlarda değil, uzayın derinliklerinde ve Ay yüzeyinde yazılmıştır.
İşte doğuşundan günümüze Omega Moonwatch hakkında bilmeniz gereken temel başlıklar:

- Yarış Pistlerinden Uzaya Başlayan Serüven
Pek çok kişinin sandığının aksine Speedmaster, başlangıçta uzay görevleri için üretilmemiştir.
 1957 Doğumu: Omega; Seamaster 300 ve Railmaster ile birlikte “Trilogy” (Üçleme) serisinin bir parçası olarak ilk Speedmaster’ı (Ref. CK2915) piyasaya sürdü.
 İlklerin Saati: Kadran yerine takimetre ölçeğini dış çerçeveye (bezel) taşıyan dünyadaki ilk kronograf saattir. Amacı yarış pilotlarının, mühendislerin ve sporcuların hız ile zaman ölçümü yapmasını kolaylaştırmaktı.

- NASA Testleri ve “Flight Qualified” Unvanı
1960’ların başında NASA, insanlı uzay görevlerinde astronotların güvenle kullanabileceği bir kronograf arayışına girdi.
 Birçok lüks saat markasının kronograf modelleri gizlice satın alınarak +93°C’den -18°C’ye ani sıcaklık değişimleri, yüksek şok, titreşim ve saf oksijen basıncı gibi ağır testlere tabi tutuldu.
 Bu zorlu ve adeta “saat işkencesi” sayılabilecek testlerden tek parça ve çalışır halde çıkan tek saat Omega Speedmaster oldu. 1 Mart 1965’te NASA tarafından tüm insanlı uzay görevleri için resmi olarak onaylandı (“Flight Qualified for all manned space missions”).

- Ay Yüzeyine İlk Adım (1969)
20 Temmuz 1969’da Apollo 11 misyonuyla insanlık Ay’a ayak bastığında, astronotların bileğinde bu saat vardı.
 İlk Ay Saati: Neil Armstrong, Ay modülünün elektronik zamanlayıcısı arızalandığı için kendi saatini modülde bırakmıştı. Bu yüzden Ay yüzeyinde fiziksel olarak ilk yürüyen saat, Buzz Aldrin’in uzay giysisinin üzerine takılı olan Speedmaster Professional Ref. 105.012 oldu. O andan itibaren saat resmi olarak “Moonwatch” lakabını kazandı.

@krayon.ch reveals Parhelion, named after a rare atmospheric phenomenon witnessed by co-founders Rémi Maillat and Fei Hou during an expedition to Greenland, where sunlight passing through suspended hexagonal ice crystals created luminous reflections beside the sun, dissolving the landscape into shifting shades of white and blue.

That same play of light continues throughout the timepiece. At 12 o’clock, a white sapphire in Krayon’s signature Y-shaped cut marks the sun at its highest point. From there, the gemstones move from white into deep blue, following the natural shift from daylight into night, while their gem-setting takes its angles from the Earth’s longitudes and latitudes.

Across the dial, eleven diamonds appear to drift above the mother-of-pearl like pieces of ice over water, changing with every movement of light.

Once again, Krayon proves that its uniqueness begins with the very foundations of time—beautifully linking its passage to the natural rhythms of the Earth.

A long overdue review of my Business Class experience with China Eastern Airlines from Paris to Shanghai. ✈️ Technically, my journey began in Geneva, connecting through Paris, and both flights featured the same beautifully designed Business Class cabin. I flew this itinerary last September as part of my birthday trip, making it my very first experience with a mainland Chinese carrier—and it genuinely exceeded my expectations. The cabin embraces a refined, contemporary aesthetic with clean lines, subtle finishes, and a sense of understated luxury. Configured in a 1-2-1 layout, every passenger enjoys direct aisle access, and as always, I opted for the window seat for maximum privacy. Beyond the hard product, what impressed me most was the overall execution. The service was attentive yet unobtrusive, the cabin felt calm and well maintained, and every element—from the seating to the dining presentation—delivered the polished experience you would expect from a premium long-haul product. Over the past few years, I’ve found myself gravitating more toward Asian airlines. There is a consistency in hospitality, attention to detail, and passenger comfort that continues to set them apart. While every airline has its own identity, the overall standard across many Asian carriers remains exceptionally high. The @glashuetteoriginal PanoMaticInverse reinterprets traditional movement architecture by bringing its mechanical complexity to the forefront. Housed in a 42 mm stainless steel case, the watch reveals its duplex swan-neck fine adjustment on the dial side, transforming a typically hidden technical feature into the visual centrepiece of the design.

Defined by the collection’s characteristic asymmetric layout, the display presents hours, minutes, small seconds, and Glashütte Original’s signature Panorama Date. To achieve this inverted construction, numerous movement components were re-engineered and repositioned, allowing elements normally viewed through the caseback to become part of the dial-side composition.

The Panorama Date remains one of the collection’s defining features, using two concentric display discs positioned on the same plane for exceptional legibility without a separating bar. The result is a watch that balances technical ingenuity with Glashütte Original’s distinctive mechanical and visual identity.

A random photo resurfaced from my iPhone today, a snapshot of my collection taken before COVID.

Back then, F.P. Journe hadn’t yet become the darling of the collecting world because it wasn’t a Patek Philippe. Even the Richard Mille RM 67-02 barely turned heads, dismissed by many for being too thin and too small.

It’s fascinating how quickly the landscape changed. Hype took over. FOMO crept in. Suddenly, the very same watches became objects of obsession and the desirables of every heart. 

It serves as a reminder of something I’ve always believed: stay true to your own passion. The most interesting watches aren’t always the ones everyone is chasing. Sometimes, the greatest discoveries lie exactly where no one else is looking.

After all, isn’t that what collecting is really about? Isn’t the journey far more rewarding than simply arriving at the destination? Why are we falling into the traps of social media today?

方寸之間盡顯從容風範——Patek Philippe 6119手動上弦腕錶

Patek Philippe Calatrava 系列是經典圓形腕錶的典範之作，而玫瑰金型號 6119R-001及白金型號6119G-001，以典雅與現代交織的風采，成為高級腕錶愛好者的心儀之選。這款腕錶採用直徑39毫米、厚度僅8.08毫米的玫瑰金錶殼或白金錶殼，纖薄輕盈，完美貼合手腕。其最引人入勝之處，莫過於錶圈上細膩雕刻的「巴黎釘紋」（Clous de Paris）璣鏤雕花，這經典菱格紋自問世以來便與Calatrava系列結下不解之緣，如今再度綻放，為寬闊的銀色粒紋錶盤賦予豐富的視覺層次與現代精緻感。

在銀色或黑色的錶盤上，金質立體刻面時標與棱角分明的太子妃式時、分針相得益彰，而位於6時位置的小秒針盤，則為簡約佈局添上一抹古典韻味。這份精緻美學更延伸至內在，兩款腕錶皆搭載了Patek Philippe研發的30-255 PS手動上弦機芯，其厚度僅2.55毫米，配備並聯雙發條盒，能確保至少65小時的動力儲存，並具備精準至秒的停秒功能。透過藍寶石水晶透明底蓋，機芯上精美的日內瓦波紋與倒角拋光修飾盡收眼底，每一處細節均符合嚴苛的百達翡麗印記 (PP Seal) 標準。巧克力棕色或黑色方形鱗紋鱷魚皮錶帶配以金質針扣，盡顯低調而華麗的氣度。

Il mito Rolex è celebrato attraverso un’importante retrospettiva sul Rolex Submariner, dalle prime referenze prive di spallette di protezione fino ai modelli neomoderni, offrendo una panoramica sull’evoluzione di uno degli orologi più iconici di sempre. Completano la selezione alcuni rari Rolex Day-Date ref. 1806 Florentine, celebri per la sofisticata lavorazione della cassa.
Accanto all’orologeria d’eccellenza, RETROFUTURE propone una raffinata selezione di alta gioielleria, con importanti pietre di colore naturali e non trattate, bracciali dal design scultoreo e spille figurative e floreali di rara bellezza, autentiche testimonianze della più alta tradizione orafa.

Ad arricchire la proposta della Maison ginevrina vi è inoltre una ricercata selezione di modelli con casse lavorate, dettagli artigianali oggi ai vertici del desiderio collezionistico internazionale
Il mito Rolex è celebrato attraverso un’importante retrospettiva sul Rolex Submariner, dalle prime referenze prive di spallette di protezione fino ai modelli neomoderni, offrendo una panoramica sull’evoluzione di uno degli orologi più iconici di sempre. Completano la selezione alcuni rari Rolex Day-Date ref. 1806 Florentine, celebri per la sofisticata lavorazione della cassa.
Accanto all’orologeria d’eccellenza, RETROFUTURE propone una raffinata selezione di alta gioielleria, con importanti pietre di colore naturali e non trattate, bracciali dal design scultoreo e spille figurative e floreali di rara bellezza, autentiche testimonianze della più alta tradizione orafa.
Una vendita pensata per collezionisti, appassionati e per chi ricerca oggetti capaci di custodire storia, stile e valore in un perfetto equilibrio tra passato e futuro.
Una collezione curata nei minimi dettagli, pensata per collezionisti esigenti, appassionati e per chiunque sia alla ricerca di oggetti capaci di attraversare le epoche custodendo immutato il proprio fascino. Sfoglia il catalog…

@krayon.ch reveals Parhelion, named after a rare atmospheric phenomenon witnessed by co-founders Rémi Maillat and Fei Hou during an expedition to Greenland, where sunlight passing through suspended hexagonal ice crystals created luminous reflections beside the sun, dissolving the landscape into shifting shades of white and blue.

That same play of light continues throughout the timepiece. At 12 o’clock, a white sapphire in Krayon’s signature Y-shaped cut marks the sun at its highest point. From there, the gemstones move from white into deep blue, following the natural shift from daylight into night, while their gem-setting takes its angles from the Earth’s longitudes and latitudes.

Across the dial, eleven diamonds appear to drift above the mother-of-pearl like pieces of ice over water, changing with every movement of light.

Once again, Krayon proves that its uniqueness begins with the very foundations of time—beautifully linking its passage to the natural rhythms of the Earth.

When Piaget introduced the Polo in 1979, it challenged the conventions of luxury sports watches at their core. At a time when the category was increasingly defined by steel cases and overt technicality, Piaget chose a different path—one rooted in precious metal, fluid form, and lifestyle elegance. The original Polo was not conceived as a tool watch, but as a confident statement where case and bracelet merged into a single, continuous object

The defining feature of the Polo was its sequence of horizontal gadroons flowing uninterrupted across the case and integrated bracelet. Rather than separating functional elements, Piaget treated the watch as a sculptural whole. This philosophy aligned naturally with the maison’s long-standing expertise in gold craftsmanship and ultra-thin watchmaking, positioning the Polo as an expression of refinement and ease rather than performance-driven utility

The modern Polo 79 revisits this idea with remarkable fidelity, and the two-tone execution adds a subtle layer of historical resonance. By pairing white gold with polished yellow-gold gadroons, the watch recalls an era when bi-metal designs conveyed confidence without excess. The contrast is deliberate yet restrained: yellow gold highlights the Polo’s signature horizontal architecture, while white gold lends a cooler, contemporary balance

Powering the Two-Tone Polo 79 is Piaget’s ultra-thin automatic calibre 1200P. Built around a micro-rotor architecture, it preserves the watch’s slender profile while maintaining mechanical reliability. More importantly, the movement reflects Piaget’s belief that technical sophistication should serve design, not overshadow it. In the Polo 79, mechanics act as an enabler of elegance, reaffirming Piaget’s vision of luxury defined by harmony, precious materials, and effortless design.

A dragon beneath the glass.

For this custom-made Georg, the movement received a full hand engraving with a dragon motif. Within the composition, a personal insignia appears: the “J-King”, a letter J crowned above.
The engraving turns the calibre into more than a mechanical construction. It becomes part of the owner’s story, carried inside the architecture of the Georg movement.
This is where individualization reaches its most intimate form: visible to those who know where to look.

Equipped with the automatic Breitling 01 calibre, this chronograph is chronometer-certified and water-resistant to 200 metres, offering reliable performance and durability for extended use in diverse environments.

At 38.5mm, the cool luster of the white gold case provides a crisp boundary for the solid silver dial, allowing the signature off-center layout and outsize date to breathe in an entirely new way.
Inside, the second-generation Calibre L121.1 offers a mechanical cadence just as refined as its face, featuring an instantaneous jumping date and the warm, golden hue of untreated German silver plates. For the collector, it represents a rare intersection: the uncompromising soul of Glashütte, captured in a rare, transient palette.

Blue was one of the most precious sources of pigment in medieval Europe.

At that time, the finest blue pigment had to be extracted from lapis lazuli, a stone transported all the way from Afghanistan, thousands of kilometers away. This blue was known as oltremarino, meaning “blue from beyond the sea,” and later as ultramarine. The name combines ultra, meaning “beyond,” with marine, meaning “the sea,” referring to a pigment that came from across the ocean.

Because of its distant origin, rarity, and great cost, ultramarine came to symbolize nobility, scarcity, divinity, and beauty.

To most people, it may seem that lapis lazuli containing “gold” would be more valuable. In reality, however, the golden flecks in lapis lazuli are not gold, but pyrite. Therefore, in the jewelry world, the most valuable lapis lazuli is not the kind with more golden specks, but the type with a rich, even blue color, no cracks, and no visible white calcite. This is considered the finest and most desirable quality.

Вдохновением для неё стали морские прогулки семьи Николая II на яхте «Штандарт» — символе утончённого вкуса, статуса и безупречной эстетики.

В сентябре 1896 года «Штандарт» стал плавучей резиденцией Романовых. Его узнаваемый облик — с позолоченным двуглавым орлом, чёрным корпусом и золотыми деталями — отражал величие и трепетное отношение к деталям. Интерьеры отличались сдержанной изысканностью: благородные породы дерева, тиснёная кожа и мягкие ткани создавали атмосферу уюта без излишней помпезности. Даже походная церковь с иконой «Хождение Иисуса Христа по водам» подчеркивала особый дух этого пространства.

Брошь «Цесаревич» в виде изящного парусника объединяет морскую свежесть и изысканность императорского стиля.

Claude André Genève was established in Geneva in 1982 by Sodimo SA, a company founded by entrepreneurs of Syrian origin. Built with Swiss craftsmanship but aimed primarily at the Levant, these watches found their home on wrists across Syria and its neighboring countries.

Then history intervened.

As the Syrian civil war unfolded, forgotten inventories began making their way into Turkey through Syrian dealers. Many arrived as genuine new old stock, untouched for decades, quietly preserved in warehouses while the world outside changed forever.

That is why a Claude André is more than a Swiss mechanical watch. It is a witness to trade, migration, resilience and the enduring ties between neighboring peoples. A reminder that even the smallest objects can carry stories far greater than themselves.

Sometimes, the most fascinating provenance is not written in a catalog.

It is written by history itself.

C’est avec une immense gratitude que j’ai appris ce matin ma nomination au grade de Chevalier de la Légion d’honneur.
Je reçois cette distinction comme un grand honneur et la partage aujourd’hui avec celles et ceux qui m’ont accompagné au fil des années. 
Cette reconnaissance m’encourage également à poursuivre les engagements portés par le fonds de dotation PerFumum au service du Parfum et de son patrimoine, et le fonds de dotation Francis Kurkdjian qui œuvre en faveur de la diversité et des publics éloignés de la Culture.
J’ai enfin une pensée émue pour mes grands-parents, survivants du génocide arménien et réfugiés en France. Leur courage, leur confiance dans leur nouvelle patrie, et les valeurs qu’ils m’ont transmises donnent à cet honneur une résonance toute particulière.
Merci pour cette reconnaissance et pour les nombreux messages de bienveillance qui m’ont profondément touché.

🔥⌚ Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Hybris Artistica Calibre 179
The Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Hybris Artistica Calibre 179 is one of the most technically insane and artistically refined watches ever created in modern haute horology. Built around the Maison’s legendary multi-axis Gyrotourbillon, the watch combines extreme mechanical engineering with hand-finished artistic craftsmanship inside the iconic reversible Reverso case. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +2
At the heart of the watch is the fourth-generation Gyrotourbillon, composed of 123 components. The inner titanium cage rotates every 16 seconds, while the outer carriage completes a full rotation every minute, creating a floating anti-gravity effect visible from both dials. The flying construction makes the mechanism appear suspended in space beneath the sapphire crystal. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Powered by the hand-wound Calibre 179, the watch uses Jaeger-LeCoultre’s patented Duoface architecture, displaying two time zones across two completely different personalities. The front dial showcases geometric black lacquer artwork inspired by Art Deco architecture, while the reverse reveals a skeletonized mechanical universe surrounding the Gyrotourbillon. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
The craftsmanship is equally extraordinary. The pink or white gold bridges are laser-cut to create nearly 200 microscopic hollows, then individually hand-lacquered by a single artisan—an art mastered by only a few craftsmen inside the manufacture. Despite containing 382 components, the case remains only 13.63mm thick. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Limited to just 10 pieces worldwide, the watch reportedly carries a value around $600,000+, placing it among the rarest and most exclusive Reversos ever made. 
Collectors on Reddit described it as “the most beautiful timepiece” they had ever seen, while others compared the floating Gyrotourbillon to “sorcery on the wrist.”

Exclusives, live. This Élégante 40 in pink gold is amongst the rarest Élégante specifications ever made. Nearly all Élégantes are titanium; a small fraction of 40-case production came in pink gold with diamond bevels and a black dial. This example is pink gold with no diamonds at all, a specification available only by special request (on a factory Karung leather strap). This listing marks a market debut—none have appeared at auction or publicly before. This is, arguably, the most graceful and luxurious of Élégantes.

In 2003, François-Paul travelled to the Middle East and found some of his collectors’ wives pining for an FP Journe of their own. Quartz suited the lifestyle requests he received, but the challenge was not taken lightly—the result proved so well executed it was later scaled up to meet the many requests from men for a larger take. FP Journe refused to simply hide a quartz movement away, instead creating one worth displaying proudly. Development of calibre 1210 ran long for the sake of a microprocessor, key to its pièce de résistance: standby mode. After 35 minutes without motion, the hands shut down. The dial opening reveals a small gold oscillating mass which ‘wakes’ the calibre when picked back up; the hands then move clockwise or counter-clockwise, whichever path is shorter, to the correct time. The result is a 10-year battery life with 18 years of standby. It even uses two separate motors for the main and seconds hands, eliminating the frictional losses of long gear trains. The base remains pink gold, with 132 components and extensive finishing.

The Élégante arrived first in this 40mm model (wearing like a circular 36mm), then a 48mm (wearing like a 40 or 41mm). The case is a modern ‘Tortue’, heavily faceted and ultra-thin at 7.35mm—and the only FP Journe with a screw-down crown. Where the titanium Élégante is a utilitarian object, this precious metal case defines a new category: aesthetically reminiscent of the Vagabondage, yet notably more petite,…

The @glashuetteoriginal PanoMaticInverse reinterprets traditional movement architecture by bringing its mechanical complexity to the forefront. Housed in a 42 mm stainless steel case, the watch reveals its duplex swan-neck fine adjustment on the dial side, transforming a typically hidden technical feature into the visual centrepiece of the design.

Defined by the collection’s characteristic asymmetric layout, the display presents hours, minutes, small seconds, and Glashütte Original’s signature Panorama Date. To achieve this inverted construction, numerous movement components were re-engineered and repositioned, allowing elements normally viewed through the caseback to become part of the dial-side composition.

The Panorama Date remains one of the collection’s defining features, using two concentric display discs positioned on the same plane for exceptional legibility without a separating bar. This gem is so rare that most gemologists and collectors never see one.

This 20.13-carat transparent pinkish-orange gemstone earned a Guinness World Record in 2025 as the world's largest faceted väyrynenite. GIA also identified the gem and issued a Monograph denoting its rarity.

Gem-quality väyrynenite remains exceptionally scarce. Miners have recovered the species in only a handful of places, including Finland, Pakistan, Afghanistan and Nigeria, and cutters have fashioned very few crystals into gemstones.

The mineral honors Finnish mineralogist Heikki Allan Väyrynen, and examples of this size and quality rank among the rarest treasures in the collector world.

🎬 Dizi: Suits
🎭 Tür: Hukuk, Dram
⭐ IMDb: 8.4/10
📺 Yayın Yılı: 2011 - 2019

Aaron Korsh tarafından yaratılan Suits, New York'un en prestijli hukuk firmalarından birinde geçen hikâyesiyle televizyon tarihinin en popüler hukuk dizilerinden biri olarak öne çıkar. Gabriel Macht'ın karizmatik performansıyla hayat verdiği Harvey Specter, özgüveni, keskin zekâsı ve kusursuz dava stratejileriyle modern televizyonun en ikonik avukat karakterlerinden biri hâline gelmiştir. Patrick J. Adams'ın canlandırdığı Mike Ross ile kurduğu sıra dışı ortaklık, Jessica Pearson, Louis Litt ve Donna Paulsen gibi unutulmaz karakterlerle birleşerek diziyi yalnızca bir hukuk draması olmaktan çıkarıp güçlü karakter gelişimine sahip bir yapıma dönüştürür.

Suits; hukuk, güç, rekabet, sadakat, hırs ve başarı temalarını sürükleyici anlatımıyla ustalıkla işler. Harvey Specter'ın her davada sergilediği stratejik hamleler, liderlik anlayışı ve kazanma tutkusu hikâyenin temelini oluştururken, Mike Ross ile arasındaki güven ilişkisi dizinin en etkileyici yönlerinden biri hâline gelir. Etkileyici diyalogları, güçlü oyuncu kadrosu ve karakter odaklı anlatımı sayesinde Suits, yıllar geçmesine rağmen en çok izlenen ve en çok konuşulan hukuk dizileri arasında yer almaya devam etmektedir.

Karizmatik karakterleri, zekâ dolu diyalogları ve unutulmaz dava hikâyelerini seviyorsanız, bu evren size eşsiz bir deneyim sunar. Bu edit, Suits hikâyesini yeniden hissetmek ve Harvey Specter'ın karizmasını, liderliğini ve kazanma tutkusunu yakından görmek isteyenler için güçlü bir görsel anlatım sunmayı hedefler.

Urban Jürgensen Reference 1140L in platinum is a masterclass in understated haute horlogerie, where every detail reflects centuries of traditional craftsmanship. Its 40 mm platinum case is distinguished by the brand’s signature hand-soldered teardrop lugs, while the solid silver dial is meticulously hand-guilloché using traditional rose-engine lathes. Multiple guilloché patterns create remarkable depth, complemented by polished white gold Breguet numerals and Urban Jürgensen’s iconic hands with their diamond-polished eye. Rather than seeking attention through complexity, the 1140L expresses refinement through perfect proportions, exceptional finishing and timeless elegance

Visible through the sapphire caseback is the hand-wound P4 calibre, developed exclusively for Urban Jürgensen. Equipped with twin barrels, it delivers a 72-hour power reserve while maintaining a classical 3 Hz beat rate. The movement exemplifies traditional finishing at the highest level, featuring radiating Geneva stripes, flawless hand-polished bevels, mirror-polished jewel sinks, thermally blued screws and an openworked balance bridge that showcases the large free-sprung balance. Every surface reflects the philosophy of independent watchmaking, where beauty is found not in excess, but in uncompromising craftsmanship. The 1140L remains one of the finest examples of a modern dress watch, combining Danish design heritage with the very best of Swiss haute horlogerie

The 1815 Rattrapante Honeygold “Homage to F. A. Lange” is a tribute to the legacy of Ferdinand Adolph Lange and to one of the most sophisticated complications in traditional watchmaking. Crafted from Lange’s proprietary Honeygold and limited to just 100 pieces, it combines classical 1815 aesthetics with the mechanical elegance of a split-seconds chronograph.

At the heart of the watch is the manually wound Calibre L101.2, featuring a rattrapante mechanism that allows multiple intermediate times to be measured during a single elapsed event. Two centrally mounted chronograph hands start together, while the upper split-seconds hand can be stopped independently to record lap times before instantly catching up with the running chronograph hand. Visible through the sapphire caseback, the movement showcases the meticulous hand-finishing and technical refinement that define A. Lange & Söhne’s approach to haute horlogerie.

One of the classic divers out there!✨ The Rolex Submariner Date is more than just one of the world’s most recognisable dive watches, it is the benchmark by which countless others are judged. Since its introduction in 1953, it has defined the modern dive watch, combining professional capability with timeless design in a way few watches have ever achieved. The current 41mm reference continues that legacy with subtle refinements that make an already iconic watch even better.

The black dial is a masterclass in legibility, with large Chromalight filled hour markers and the signature Mercedes hands delivering exceptional clarity in all conditions. Surrounding it is the black Cerachrom ceramic bezel, virtually scratch resistant and engineered for precise dive timing. The combination of the glossy black dial, ceramic bezel, and Oystersteel case creates a look that is instantly recognisable, equally at home beneath the waves or paired with everyday attire.

The 41mm Oystersteel case feels robust yet perfectly balanced on the wrist. Fitted with the Oyster bracelet, Oysterlock safety clasp, and Rolex’s ingenious Glidelock extension system, it offers exceptional comfort with effortless micro-adjustment, making it one of the finest bracelet and clasp combinations in the industry. With 300 metres of water resistance, the Submariner remains every bit the professional dive watch it was designed to be.

Powering the watch is Rolex’s in house Calibre 3235, a Superlative Chronometer movement featuring the blue Parachrom hairspring, Paraflex shock absorbers, and an impressive 70 hour power reserve. Combining outstanding reliability, precision, and durability, it perfectly complements a watch that has become one of the greatest icons in modern watchmaking, a true tool watch that continues to set the standard. 💫

Today, a visionary has left us, but his vision will remain forever in the heart, soul, and the country he was born to, lived in, and cherished deeply. Today, the father has left us, but he is not gone.

I am deeply saddened by the passing of His Highness the Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, who was a special person, a mentor, a visionary, and someone I was very close to.

Although he will be greatly missed in Qatar and around the world, his great life should be celebrated for its many achievements. During his 18 years as the ruler of Qatar, he played a pivotal role in the country’s development and helped shape it into the remarkable nation it is today. I feel fortunate to have spent valuable time in his company. He was always inspiring, kind, and gracious in everything he did.
He taught me that vision is not only words; it is actions to be taken, a stand to be taken, a truth to be spoken. Thank you for welcoming me into your beautiful country. Thank you for making me feel at home.

Thanks to your contagious love for this beautiful Qatar, I fell in love as well, and it became my home, my country.

Yesterday, Qatar was the home of millions celebrating the World Cup, thanks to his determination and a vision bigger than all of us. Today, Qatar is the home of all these nations, welcomed with love, generosity, and the dignity of the Qatari people. Today, we mourn a visionary, but we also celebrate a vision that will stay in the memory and the hearts of everyone.

My heart, thoughts, and prayers are with His Highness the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the entire Al Thani family, and all the people of Qatar at this time.

May he rest in peace, and may his vision serve as a lesson for future generations.

Rest in peace, and may we find ours.

content.title: So hard for me to wear anything else when I have this

content.description:
A random photo resurfaced from my iPhone today, a snapshot of my collection taken before COVID.

Back then, F.P. Journe hadn’t yet become the darling of the collecting world because it wasn’t a Patek Philippe. Even the Richard Mille RM 67-02 barely turned heads, dismissed by many for being too thin and too small.

It’s fascinating how quickly the landscape changed. Hype took over. FOMO crept in. Suddenly, the very same watches became objects of obsession and the desirables of every heart. 

It serves as a reminder of something I’ve always believed: stay true to your own passion. The most interesting watches aren’t always the ones everyone is chasing. Sometimes, the greatest discoveries lie exactly where no one else is looking.

After all, isn’t that what collecting is really about? Isn’t the journey far more rewarding than simply arriving at the destination? Why are we falling into the traps of social media today?

The @krayon.ch Parhelion takes the brand’s Anywhere sunrise-sunset complication and covers it in 159 baguette-cut sapphires—across the bezel, midcase, lugs, and even the pin buckle—in a gradient from white to blue inspired by a trip to Greenland. The hour markers are Krayon-cut white diamonds in invisible settings on a light blue mother-of-pearl dial, and the Caliber C030 still delivers the full Anywhere display underneath all of it. For all the details from @tantantalum, head to Hodinkee.

@krayon.ch reveals Parhelion, named after a rare atmospheric phenomenon witnessed by co-founders Rémi Maillat and Fei Hou during an expedition to Greenland, where sunlight passing through suspended hexagonal ice crystals created luminous reflections beside the sun, dissolving the landscape into shifting shades of white and blue.

That same play of light continues throughout the timepiece. At 12 o’clock, a white sapphire in Krayon’s signature Y-shaped cut marks the sun at its highest point. From there, the gemstones move from white into deep blue, following the natural shift from daylight into night, while their gem-setting takes its angles from the Earth’s longitudes and latitudes.

Across the dial, eleven diamonds appear to drift above the mother-of-pearl like pieces of ice over water, changing with every movement of light.

Once again, Krayon proves that its uniqueness begins with the very foundations of time—beautifully linking its passage to the natural rhythms of the Earth.

content.description:
When Piaget introduced the Polo in 1979, it challenged the conventions of luxury sports watches at their core. At a time when the category was increasingly defined by steel cases and overt technicality, Piaget chose a different path—one rooted in precious metal, fluid form, and lifestyle elegance. The original Polo was not conceived as a tool watch, but as a confident statement where case and bracelet merged into a single, continuous object

The defining feature of the Polo was its sequence of horizontal gadroons flowing uninterrupted across the case and integrated bracelet. Rather than separating functional elements, Piaget treated the watch as a sculptural whole. This philosophy aligned naturally with the maison’s long-standing expertise in gold craftsmanship and ultra-thin watchmaking, positioning the Polo as an expression of refinement and ease rather than performance-driven utility

The modern Polo 79 revisits this idea with remarkable fidelity, and the two-tone execution adds a subtle layer of historical resonance. By pairing white gold with polished yellow-gold gadroons, the watch recalls an era when bi-metal designs conveyed confidence without excess. The contrast is deliberate yet restrained: yellow gold highlights the Polo’s signature horizontal architecture, while white gold lends a cooler, contemporary balance

Powering the Two-Tone Polo 79 is Piaget’s ultra-thin automatic calibre 1200P. Built around a micro-rotor architecture, it preserves the watch’s slender profile while maintaining mechanical reliability. More importantly, the movement reflects Piaget’s belief that technical sophistication should serve design, not overshadow it. In the Polo 79, mechanics act as an enabler of elegance, reaffirming Piaget’s vision of luxury defined by harmony, precious materials, and effortless design.

The @glashuetteoriginal PanoMaticInverse reinterprets traditional movement architecture by bringing its mechanical complexity to the forefront. Housed in a 42 mm stainless steel case, the watch reveals its duplex swan-neck fine adjustment on the dial side, transforming a typically hidden technical feature into the visual centrepiece of the design.

Defined by the collection’s characteristic asymmetric layout, the display presents hours, minutes, small seconds, and Glashütte Original’s signature Panorama Date. To achieve this inverted construction, numerous movement components were re-engineered and repositioned, allowing elements normally viewed through the caseback to become part of the dial-side composition.

The Panorama Date remains one of the collection’s defining features, using two concentric display discs positioned on the same plane for exceptional legibility without a separating bar. The result is a watch that balances technical ingenuity with Glashütte Original’s distinctive mechanical and visual identity.

Blue was one of the most precious sources of pigment in medieval Europe.

At that time, the finest blue pigment had to be extracted from lapis lazuli, a stone transported all the way from Afghanistan, thousands of kilometers away. This blue was known as oltremarino, meaning “blue from beyond the sea,” and later as ultramarine. The name combines ultra, meaning “beyond,” with marine, meaning “the sea,” referring to a pigment that came from across the ocean.

Because of its distant origin, rarity, and great cost, ultramarine came to symbolize nobility, scarcity, divinity, and beauty.

To most people, it may seem that lapis lazuli containing “gold” would be more valuable. In reality, however, the golden flecks in lapis lazuli are not gold, but pyrite. Therefore, in the jewelry world, the most valuable lapis lazuli is not the kind with more golden specks, but the type with a rich, even blue color, no cracks, and no visible white calcite. This is considered the finest and most desirable quality.

The 1815 Rattrapante Honeygold “Homage to F. A. Lange” is a tribute to the legacy of Ferdinand Adolph Lange and to one of the most sophisticated complications in traditional watchmaking. Crafted from Lange’s proprietary Honeygold and limited to just 100 pieces, it combines classical 1815 aesthetics with the mechanical elegance of a split-seconds chronograph.

At the heart of the watch is the manually wound Calibre L101.2, featuring a rattrapante mechanism that allows multiple intermediate times to be measured during a single elapsed event. Two centrally mounted chronograph hands start together, while the upper split-seconds hand can be stopped independently to record lap times before instantly catching up with the running chronograph hand. Visible through the sapphire caseback, the movement showcases the meticulous hand-finishing and technical refinement that define A. Lange & Söhne’s approach to haute horlogerie.

Urban Jürgensen Reference 1140L in platinum is a masterclass in understated haute horlogerie, where every detail reflects centuries of traditional craftsmanship. Its 40 mm platinum case is distinguished by the brand’s signature hand-soldered teardrop lugs, while the solid silver dial is meticulously hand-guilloché using traditional rose-engine lathes. Multiple guilloché patterns create remarkable depth, complemented by polished white gold Breguet numerals and Urban Jürgensen’s iconic hands with their diamond-polished eye. Rather than seeking attention through complexity, the 1140L expresses refinement through perfect proportions, exceptional finishing and timeless elegance

Visible through the sapphire caseback is the hand-wound P4 calibre, developed exclusively for Urban Jürgensen. Equipped with twin barrels, it delivers a 72-hour power reserve while maintaining a classical 3 Hz beat rate. The movement exemplifies traditional finishing at the highest level, featuring radiating Geneva stripes, flawless hand-polished bevels, mirror-polished jewel sinks, thermally blued screws and an openworked balance bridge that showcases the large free-sprung balance. Every surface reflects the philosophy of independent watchmaking, where beauty is found not in excess, but in uncompromising craftsmanship. The 1140L remains one of the finest examples of a modern dress watch, combining Danish design heritage with the very best of Swiss haute horlogerie

The first VPC model to sell out was Type 37HW in Dove Grey.

We work in small batches of continuously evolving watches. This means that, once a batch is sold out, it is gone forever and moves to the VPC Archive on our website. This isn't intended as some false scarcity model or to trigger FOMO. Frankly, the watch market is far too cooled-off for that at the moment, so even if I wanted to, it wouldn't work. 

Instead, VPC is a creative endeavor for me. I have no interest in growing the company too much and pushing big numbers of watches. To me, the value lies in continuously dreaming up and developing truly special watches and executing them to an extremely high standard. This means each batch builds on the previous, evolving it in some small or large way. The fact that this makes each batch a little more special to the enthusiasts who own them is a great bonus. 

That's not to say I will never do anything like this again. Type 37HW will surely come back, but with different dials at the very least. In fact...I have a very small run of something exotic in the works. Subscribe to the newsletter on the website to be the first to know!

Exclusives, live. This Élégante 40 in pink gold is amongst the rarest Élégante specifications ever made. Nearly all Élégantes are titanium; a small fraction of 40-case production came in pink gold with diamond bevels and a black dial. This example is pink gold with no diamonds at all, a specification available only by special request (on a factory Karung leather strap). This listing marks a market debut—none have appeared at auction or publicly before. This is, arguably, the most graceful and luxurious of Élégantes.

In 2003, François-Paul travelled to the Middle East and found some of his collectors’ wives pining for an FP Journe of their own. Quartz suited the lifestyle requests he received, but the challenge was not taken lightly—the result proved so well executed it was later scaled up to meet the many requests from men for a larger take. FP Journe refused to simply hide a quartz movement away, instead creating one worth displaying proudly. Development of calibre 1210 ran long for the sake of a microprocessor, key to its pièce de résistance: standby mode. After 35 minutes without motion, the hands shut down. The dial opening reveals a small gold oscillating mass which ‘wakes’ the calibre when picked back up; the hands then move clockwise or counter-clockwise, whichever path is shorter, to the correct time. The result is a 10-year battery life with 18 years of standby. It even uses two separate motors for the main and seconds hands, eliminating the frictional losses of long gear trains. The base remains pink gold, with 132 components and extensive finishing.

The Élégante arrived first in this 40mm model (wearing like a circular 36mm), then a 48mm (wearing like a 40 or 41mm). The case is a modern ‘Tortue’, heavily faceted and ultra-thin at 7.35mm—and the only FP Journe with a screw-down crown. Where the titanium Élégante is a utilitarian object, this precious metal case defines a new category: aesthetically reminiscent of the Vagabondage, yet notably more petite,…

Apple is expected to unveil its iPhone 18 lineup in the coming months, although the company has yet to officially confirm any details. iPhone 18 Pro Max Could Get a Bigger Battery and New Colours

According to tipster Ice Universe, the Chinese variant of the iPhone 18 Pro Max may feature a 5,500mAh battery, making it the largest battery ever in an iPhone. The larger cell could result in a thicker design, with the handset reportedly measuring around 9mm in thickness and weighing close to 240g. Apple is also tipped to introduce four new colour options for the Pro lineup: Dark Cherry, Light Blue, Silver, and Dark Gray.

Display May Get a Smaller Dynamic Island

Apple is expected to retain the 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch display sizes for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, respectively. However, the company could reduce the size of the Dynamic Island by up to 35 percent, offering more screen space. The displays are also rumoured to adopt LTPO+ technology, which could improve power efficiency and contribute to better battery life.

Camera Could Add Variable Aperture Lens

The iPhone 18 Pro series is expected to carry over much of its existing camera hardware while introducing a manual variable-aperture system for the primary camera. The inner titanium cage rotates every 16 seconds, while the outer carriage completes a full rotation every minute, creating a floating anti-gravity effect visible from both dials. The flying construction makes the mechanism appear suspended in space beneath the sapphire crystal. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Powered by the hand-wound Calibre 179, the watch uses Jaeger-LeCoultre’s patented Duoface architecture, displaying two time zones across two completely different personalities. The front dial showcases geometric black lacquer artwork inspired by Art Deco architecture, while the reverse reveals a skeletonized mechanical universe surrounding the Gyrotourbillon. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
The craftsmanship is equally extraordinary. The pink or white gold bridges are laser-cut to create nearly 200 microscopic hollows, then individually hand-lacquered by a single artisan—an art mastered by only a few craftsmen inside the manufacture. Despite containing 382 components, the case remains only 13.63mm thick. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Limited to just 10 pieces worldwide, the watch reportedly carries a value around $600,000+, placing it among the rarest and most exclusive Reversos ever made. 
Collectors on Reddit described it as “the most beautiful timepiece” they had ever seen, while others compared the floating Gyrotourbillon to “sorcery on the wrist.”

Para mim, o número 2 mais bonito da relojoaria. Mas a verdade é que a tipografia inteira da Lange merece esse título. 

A escolha de uma fonte é uma questão mais complicada do que parece. O peso, o espaçamento e o uso (ou não) de serifa falam muito sobre a personalidade e a primeira impressão que temos de um relógio. 

Além do layout perfeitamente assimétrico do Lange 1, o que sempre me chamou atenção foi sua tipografia, especialmente na “outize date”, como a marca gosta de chamar, e no logotipo. Claro que não pude deixar de ir atrás e entender de onde vinha aquilo. 

A base é uma adaptação da clássica Engravers, uma tipografia originalmente criada para servir de guia a gravadores em metal. A Lange reinterpretou essa linguagem para criar uma identidade clássica, robusta e extremamente refinada. Já o “&” do logotipo foi completamente redesenhado. 

Agora, sobre o “25” que sempre me encanta, existe outra curiosidade: já reparou que em praticamente todos os catálogos e fotos oficiais da Lange os relógios mostram a data 25?

O motivo remete a 24 de outubro de 1994, quando Walter Lange apresentou ao mundo a primeira coleção da manufatura renascida.

Como as fotografias do evento seriam publicadas apenas no dia seguinte pelos jornais, ele pediu que todos os relógios fossem ajustados para o dia 25, para que as imagens já mostrassem a data correta do lançamento quando chegassem às mídias.

O detalhe permaneceu e até hoje, em catálogo, a data está ajustada no dia 25.

14 LUGLIO 2026
ASTA DI OROLOGI E GIOIELLI

RETROFUTURE celebra l’armonioso connubio tra modernità e classicismo, un dialogo incessante in cui l’innovazione sposa la tradizione. In questa selezione, la maestria del passato sembra reinterpretata attraverso la lente della contemporaneità, arricchita da quella preziosa patina del tempo. 
Tra i lotti più significativi spiccano straordinari capolavori del tempo, a partire da una superba antologia di Patek Philippe Calatrava. Tra questi, brilla per assoluta rarità uno storico Calibro 96 con cassa in acciaio e indici applicati in oro rosa: una configurazione di straordinaria ed eccezionale rarità, confermata ufficialmente dall’Estratto d’Archivio. Ad arricchire la proposta della Maison ginevrina vi è inoltre una ricercata selezione di modelli con casse lavorate, dettagli artigianali oggi ai vertici del desiderio collezionistico internazionale
Il mito Rolex è celebrato attraverso un’importante retrospettiva sul Rolex Submariner, dalle prime referenze prive di spallette di protezione fino ai modelli neomoderni, offrendo una panoramica sull’evoluzione di uno degli orologi più iconici di sempre. Completano la selezione alcuni rari Rolex Day-Date ref. 1806 Florentine, celebri per la sofisticata lavorazione della cassa.
Accanto all’orologeria d’eccellenza, RETROFUTURE propone una raffinata selezione di alta gioielleria, con importanti pietre di colore naturali e non trattate, bracciali dal design scultoreo e spille figurative e floreali di rara bellezza, autentiche testimonianze della più alta tradizione orafa.
Una vendita pensata per collezionisti, appassionati e per chi ricerca oggetti capaci di custodire storia, stile e valore in un perfetto equilibrio tra passato e futuro.
Una collezione curata nei minimi dettagli, pensata per collezionisti esigenti, appassionati e per chiunque sia alla ricerca di oggetti capaci di attraversare le epoche custodendo immutato il proprio fascino. Sfoglia il catalog…

C’est avec une immense gratitude que j’ai appris ce matin ma nomination au grade de Chevalier de la Légion d’honneur.
Je reçois cette distinction comme un grand honneur et la partage aujourd’hui avec celles et ceux qui m’ont accompagné au fil des années. 
Cette reconnaissance m’encourage également à poursuivre les engagements portés par le fonds de dotation PerFumum au service du Parfum et de son patrimoine, et le fonds de dotation Francis Kurkdjian qui œuvre en faveur de la diversité et des publics éloignés de la Culture.
J’ai enfin une pensée émue pour mes grands-parents, survivants du génocide arménien et réfugiés en France. Leur courage, leur confiance dans leur nouvelle patrie, et les valeurs qu’ils m’ont transmises donnent à cet honneur une résonance toute particulière.
Merci pour cette reconnaissance et pour les nombreux messages de bienveillance qui m’ont profondément touché.

Paris St-Germain have opened talks to re-sign Aston Villa full-back Lucas Digne.

The 32-year-old is believed to have an unspecified release clause in his contract, reportedly worth over £8.5m, leaving Villa powerless to resist offers above a certain fee.

Digne would welcome a return to the back-to-back Champions League winners, where he was under contract between 2013 and 2016.

The move could see him compete with Nuno Mendes for a place in the starting line-up at Parc des Princes.

The France international is currently away with his national team at the World Cup and is set to face Spain on Tuesday.

His departure would be another blow for Villa after midfielder Youri Tielemans entered advanced talks with Manchester United. The Belgian is also understood to have a £35m release clause in his contract.

Villa have so far signed Modou Keba Cisse from Austrian club LASK and seen Donyell Malen make his loan move to Roma permanent with Enzo Barrenechea and Louie Barry also leaving on permanent deals.

Digne joined Villa from Everton in 2022 for £25m and has made 182 appearances for Unai Emery’s Europa League winners.

Omega Moonwatch Brothers 🧲🌘🚀

Saat dünyasının en büyük efsanelerinden biri olan Omega Speedmaster “Moonwatch”, horoloji tarihinin en ikonik kronografıdır. Onun hikayesi sadece laboratuvarlarda değil, uzayın derinliklerinde ve Ay yüzeyinde yazılmıştır.
İşte doğuşundan günümüze Omega Moonwatch hakkında bilmeniz gereken temel başlıklar:

- Yarış Pistlerinden Uzaya Başlayan Serüven
Pek çok kişinin sandığının aksine Speedmaster, başlangıçta uzay görevleri için üretilmemiştir.
 1957 Doğumu: Omega; Seamaster 300 ve Railmaster ile birlikte “Trilogy” (Üçleme) serisinin bir parçası olarak ilk Speedmaster’ı (Ref. CK2915) piyasaya sürdü.
 İlklerin Saati: Kadran yerine takimetre ölçeğini dış çerçeveye (bezel) taşıyan dünyadaki ilk kronograf saattir. Amacı yarış pilotlarının, mühendislerin ve sporcuların hız ile zaman ölçümü yapmasını kolaylaştırmaktı.

- NASA Testleri ve “Flight Qualified” Unvanı
1960’ların başında NASA, insanlı uzay görevlerinde astronotların güvenle kullanabileceği bir kronograf arayışına girdi.
 Birçok lüks saat markasının kronograf modelleri gizlice satın alınarak +93°C’den -18°C’ye ani sıcaklık değişimleri, yüksek şok, titreşim ve saf oksijen basıncı gibi ağır testlere tabi tutuldu.
 Bu zorlu ve adeta “saat işkencesi” sayılabilecek testlerden tek parça ve çalışır halde çıkan tek saat Omega Speedmaster oldu. 1 Mart 1965’te NASA tarafından tüm insanlı uzay görevleri için resmi olarak onaylandı (“Flight Qualified for all manned space missions”).

- Ay Yüzeyine İlk Adım (1969)
20 Temmuz 1969’da Apollo 11 misyonuyla insanlık Ay’a ayak bastığında, astronotların bileğinde bu saat vardı.
 İlk Ay Saati: Neil Armstrong, Ay modülünün elektronik zamanlayıcısı arızalandığı için kendi saatini modülde bırakmıştı. Bu yüzden Ay yüzeyinde fiziksel olarak ilk yürüyen saat, Buzz Aldrin’in uzay giysisinin üzerine takılı olan Speedmaster Professional Ref. 105.012 oldu. O andan itibaren saat resmi olarak “Moonwatch” lakabını kazandı.

Немецкий автопром заслуженно считается фундаментом мировой автомобильной индустрии, ведь именно в Германии в конце девятнадцатого века Карл Бенц и Готлиб Даймлер изобрели первый автомобиль. С тех пор немецкие машины стали глобальным эталоном инженерной точности, качества сборки и технического совершенства. На современном этапе отрасль проходит через самую масштабную трансформацию в своей истории, постепенно смещая фокус с традиционных двигателей внутреннего сгорания на электрические силовые установки и цифровые технологии. Немецкие бренды, такие как Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi и Porsche, сохраняют за собой лидерство в премиальном сегменте, предлагая покупателям не просто средство передвижения, но и передовые системы безопасности, комфорта и динамики. Сегодня производство активно перестраивается под экологические стандарты, что привело к появлению целых семейств электромобилей и гибридов, способных конкурировать с новыми игроками рынка. В 2026 году немецкая промышленность продолжает укреплять позиции второго по величине мирового центра производства электрокаров, делая ставку на высокотехнологичные батареи и восьмисотвольтовые системы быстрой зарядки. Несмотря на серьезные вызовы, такие как высокая конкуренция со стороны азиатских производителей и необходимость полной цифровизации, Германия остается колыбелью инноваций. Автопроизводители активно инвестируют в разработку автономного вождения и программного обеспечения, превращая современные машины в «компьютеры на колесах». Экспортный потенциал отрасли остается высоким, при этом компании все чаще локализуют свои исследовательские центры за рубежом, чтобы быстрее адаптироваться к запросам глобального рынка и сохранять звание мирового технологического лидера.

Claude André Genève was established in Geneva in 1982 by Sodimo SA, a company founded by entrepreneurs of Syrian origin. Built with Swiss craftsmanship but aimed primarily at the Levant, these watches found their home on wrists across Syria and its neighboring countries.

Then history intervened.

As the Syrian civil war unfolded, forgotten inventories began making their way into Turkey through Syrian dealers. Many arrived as genuine new old stock, untouched for decades, quietly preserved in warehouses while the world outside changed forever.

That is why a Claude André is more than a Swiss mechanical watch. It is a witness to trade, migration, resilience and the enduring ties between neighboring peoples. A reminder that even the smallest objects can carry stories far greater than themselves.

Sometimes, the most fascinating provenance is not written in a catalog.

It is written by history itself.

Urban Jürgensen Reference 1140L in platinum is a masterclass in understated haute horlogerie, where every detail reflects centuries of traditional craftsmanship. Its 40 mm platinum case is distinguished by the brand’s signature hand-soldered teardrop lugs, while the solid silver dial is meticulously hand-guilloché using traditional rose-engine lathes. Multiple guilloché patterns create remarkable depth, complemented by polished white gold Breguet numerals and Urban Jürgensen’s iconic hands with their diamond-polished eye. Rather than seeking attention through complexity, the 1140L expresses refinement through perfect proportions, exceptional finishing and timeless elegance

Visible through the sapphire caseback is the hand-wound P4 calibre, developed exclusively for Urban Jürgensen. Equipped with twin barrels, it delivers a 72-hour power reserve while maintaining a classical 3 Hz beat rate. The movement exemplifies traditional finishing at the highest level, featuring radiating Geneva stripes, flawless hand-polished bevels, mirror-polished jewel sinks, thermally blued screws and an openworked balance bridge that showcases the large free-sprung balance. Every surface reflects the philosophy of independent watchmaking, where beauty is found not in excess, but in uncompromising craftsmanship. The 1140L remains one of the finest examples of a modern dress watch, combining Danish design heritage with the very best of Swiss haute horlogerie

Abraham-Louis Breguet was granted a patent for the tourbillon on 26 June 1801. In other words, 225 years ago today.
The image shows the first watch I ever made. Although the dial is marked ‘001/003’, this was actually the only one I ever made, and I still have it in my possession. I regard this as a practice piece.
When I was making this tourbillon, I was simply interested in the process of making it; it never even crossed my mind that this might become my future livelihood—that I would become a watchmaker.
Whilst working on this watch and researching the tourbillon, I realised that the date the patent came into effect was the same as my birthday.
Watchmaking can be gruelling at times, but I think that fact gave me a little encouragement.

Bazı villalar doğanın içine saklanır.
Bazıları ise şehrin ışıklarını kendi manzarasına dönüştürür.

Aeris Horizon Villa, yoğun metropol silüetine bakan yüksek bir tepede konumlanan, tamamen özel yaşam hissi üzerine kurgulanmış ultra lüks bir villa konsepti olarak tasarlandı.

Bu projede amaç, bir rezidans ya da yüksek katlı yapı etkisi yaratmak değil; şehrin enerjisini uzaktan izleyen, kendi bahçesi, havuzu, terasları ve iç avlularıyla bağımsız bir yaşam senaryosu kuran özel bir villa atmosferi oluşturmaktı.

Yapının ana dili; smoked glass yüzeyler, champagne bronze detaylar, warm ivory stone kütleler, polished travertine teraslar ve reflective black stone dokular üzerinden ilerliyor. Gündüzleri cam yüzeyler şehir ışığını ve gökyüzünü yansıtırken, akşam saatlerinde içeriden gelen sıcak amber ışık villaya daha davetkâr ve sinematik bir karakter kazandırıyor.

Aeris Horizon Villa’nın en güçlü tarafı, şehirle doğrudan temas kurması ama onun karmaşasının içine karışmaması. Manzara her odanın bir parçası; fakat yapı kendi sınırlarını, kendi sessizliğini ve kendi özel atmosferini koruyor.

Dış cephede yatay kütleler, geniş konsollar, bronz hatlar ve büyük cam açıklıklar güçlü bir modern lüks dili yaratıyor. İç mekânlarda ise traverten zeminler, onyx yüzeyler, ceviz detaylar, füme cam ve yumuşak aydınlatma daha sakin, rafine ve yaşanabilir bir atmosfer oluşturuyor.

Bu konseptte lüks, sadece pahalı malzemelerle anlatılmıyor.
Lüks burada; şehrin ışıklarına bakan bir salonda, havuz yüzeyindeki yansımada, bronz detayların gün batımıyla değişen tonunda ve gece olduğunda villanın içinden dışarıya yayılan o kontrollü sıcaklıkta saklı.

A random photo resurfaced from my iPhone today, a snapshot of my collection taken before COVID.

Back then, F.P. Journe hadn’t yet become the darling of the collecting world because it wasn’t a Patek Philippe. Even the Richard Mille RM 67-02 barely turned heads, dismissed by many for being too thin and too small.

It’s fascinating how quickly the landscape changed. Hype took over. FOMO crept in. Suddenly, the very same watches became objects of obsession and the desirables of every heart. 

It serves as a reminder of something I’ve always believed: stay true to your own passion. The most interesting watches aren’t always the ones everyone is chasing. Sometimes, the greatest discoveries lie exactly where no one else is looking.

After all, isn’t that what collecting is really about? Isn’t the journey far more rewarding than simply arriving at the destination? Why are we falling into the traps of social media today?

Traveling with my daughter always reminds me that the most extraordinary experiences aren’t always about discovering new places, they’re about discovering them through their eyes.

Every place becomes an adventure. Every monument sparks a hundred questions. Every moment carries a sense of wonder that, somewhere along the way, we adults tend to lose.

In many ways, that’s exactly how I feel about my @de_bethune DB28 XP Steel Wheels. It’s a watch I’ve spent countless hours with, yet every time I put it on my wrist, I notice a detail I hadn’t appreciated before: the architecture of the movement, the interplay of light, the flawless finishing, the mechanical poetry beneath the sapphire dial.

Some companions don’t become less interesting with time; they reveal themselves layer by layer.

One reminds me to stay curious. The other reminds me why curiosity matters.

C’est avec une immense gratitude que j’ai appris ce matin ma nomination au grade de Chevalier de la Légion d’honneur.
Je reçois cette distinction comme un grand honneur et la partage aujourd’hui avec celles et ceux qui m’ont accompagné au fil des années. 
Cette reconnaissance m’encourage également à poursuivre les engagements portés par le fonds de dotation PerFumum au service du Parfum et de son patrimoine, et le fonds de dotation Francis Kurkdjian qui œuvre en faveur de la diversité et des publics éloignés de la Culture.
J’ai enfin une pensée émue pour mes grands-parents, survivants du génocide arménien et réfugiés en France. Leur courage, leur confiance dans leur nouvelle patrie, et les valeurs qu’ils m’ont transmises donnent à cet honneur une résonance toute particulière.
Merci pour cette reconnaissance et pour les nombreux messages de bienveillance qui m’ont profondément touché.

Available - More than a skeleton. A story in motion.

At first glance, you see an openworked movement.

Then your eyes catch the micro-rotor.

Shaped like the Demoiselle, the legendary aircraft designed by Alberto Santos-Dumont, it transforms every movement of the wrist into a tribute to one of aviation’s greatest pioneers.

Crafted in rose gold, the Santos-Dumont Skeleton Micro-Rotor blends mechanical ingenuity with artistic storytelling like few watches ever have.

Every detail has a purpose.

Every rotation tells a story.

What’s your favourite detail?

This was one of my faves and the main reason was that it felt like it was the closest that I could get to owning a Ref:2499/100 for considerably less funds. The Ref:3970 is to me the last great perpetual calendar chrono from the lineage of 1518 and 2499 and this is where I feel the design and manufacture were more human than computer based, like today’s offerings.

@krayon.ch reveals Parhelion, named after a rare atmospheric phenomenon witnessed by co-founders Rémi Maillat and Fei Hou during an expedition to Greenland, where sunlight passing through suspended hexagonal ice crystals created luminous reflections beside the sun, dissolving the landscape into shifting shades of white and blue.

That same play of light continues throughout the timepiece. At 12 o’clock, a white sapphire in Krayon’s signature Y-shaped cut marks the sun at its highest point. From there, the gemstones move from white into deep blue, following the natural shift from daylight into night, while their gem-setting takes its angles from the Earth’s longitudes and latitudes.

Across the dial, eleven diamonds appear to drift above the mother-of-pearl like pieces of ice over water, changing with every movement of light.

Once again, Krayon proves that its uniqueness begins with the very foundations of time—beautifully linking its passage to the natural rhythms of the Earth.

There is an architectural serenity to the Lange 1 that has remained virtually unmatched for over three decades. But when rendered in this deep, matte Prussian blue, its mathematical precision takes on a distinctly poetic character.
The Reference 191.028—part of a highly coveted, single-year run from 2017—is a masterclass in balanced contrast. At 38.5mm, the cool luster of the white gold case provides a crisp boundary for the solid silver dial, allowing the signature off-center layout and outsize date to breathe in an entirely new way.
Inside, the second-generation Calibre L121.1 offers a mechanical cadence just as refined as its face, featuring an instantaneous jumping date and the warm, golden hue of untreated German silver plates. For the collector, it represents a rare intersection: the uncompromising soul of Glashütte, captured in a rare, transient palette.

🔥⌚ Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Hybris Artistica Calibre 179
The Jaeger-LeCoultre Reverso Hybris Artistica Calibre 179 is one of the most technically insane and artistically refined watches ever created in modern haute horology. Built around the Maison’s legendary multi-axis Gyrotourbillon, the watch combines extreme mechanical engineering with hand-finished artistic craftsmanship inside the iconic reversible Reverso case. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +2
At the heart of the watch is the fourth-generation Gyrotourbillon, composed of 123 components. The inner titanium cage rotates every 16 seconds, while the outer carriage completes a full rotation every minute, creating a floating anti-gravity effect visible from both dials. The flying construction makes the mechanism appear suspended in space beneath the sapphire crystal. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Powered by the hand-wound Calibre 179, the watch uses Jaeger-LeCoultre’s patented Duoface architecture, displaying two time zones across two completely different personalities. The front dial showcases geometric black lacquer artwork inspired by Art Deco architecture, while the reverse reveals a skeletonized mechanical universe surrounding the Gyrotourbillon. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
The craftsmanship is equally extraordinary. The pink or white gold bridges are laser-cut to create nearly 200 microscopic hollows, then individually hand-lacquered by a single artisan—an art mastered by only a few craftsmen inside the manufacture. Despite containing 382 components, the case remains only 13.63mm thick. �
Jaeger-LeCoultre Press +1
Limited to just 10 pieces worldwide, the watch reportedly carries a value around $600,000+, placing it among the rarest and most exclusive Reversos ever made. 
Collectors on Reddit described it as “the most beautiful timepiece” they had ever seen, while others compared the floating Gyrotourbillon to “sorcery on the wrist.”

When Piaget introduced the Polo in 1979, it challenged the conventions of luxury sports watches at their core. At a time when the category was increasingly defined by steel cases and overt technicality, Piaget chose a different path—one rooted in precious metal, fluid form, and lifestyle elegance. The original Polo was not conceived as a tool watch, but as a confident statement where case and bracelet merged into a single, continuous object

The defining feature of the Polo was its sequence of horizontal gadroons flowing uninterrupted across the case and integrated bracelet. Rather than separating functional elements, Piaget treated the watch as a sculptural whole. This philosophy aligned naturally with the maison’s long-standing expertise in gold craftsmanship and ultra-thin watchmaking, positioning the Polo as an expression of refinement and ease rather than performance-driven utility

The modern Polo 79 revisits this idea with remarkable fidelity, and the two-tone execution adds a subtle layer of historical resonance. By pairing white gold with polished yellow-gold gadroons, the watch recalls an era when bi-metal designs conveyed confidence without excess. The contrast is deliberate yet restrained: yellow gold highlights the Polo’s signature horizontal architecture, while white gold lends a cooler, contemporary balance

Powering the Two-Tone Polo 79 is Piaget’s ultra-thin automatic calibre 1200P. Built around a micro-rotor architecture, it preserves the watch’s slender profile while maintaining mechanical reliability. More importantly, the movement reflects Piaget’s belief that technical sophistication should serve design, not overshadow it. In the Polo 79, mechanics act as an enabler of elegance, reaffirming Piaget’s vision of luxury defined by harmony, precious materials, and effortless design.

Heute feiere ich nicht nur meinen Geburtstag. Heute feiere ich den Weg, der mich hierhergeführt hat.

44 Jahre. Ein Leben, geprägt von Entscheidungen. Manche waren genau richtig, andere schmerzhaft. Doch jede einzelne hat mich zu dem Menschen gemacht, der ich heute bin. Denn Erfolg entsteht nicht dadurch, dass man niemals fällt. Erfolg entsteht, wenn man den Mut hat, immer wieder aufzustehen und weiterzugehen.

Die vergangenen Jahre haben mir eine der wertvollsten Lektionen geschenkt: Alles hat seine Zeit.

Es gibt Zeiten, in denen man kämpfen muss. Und es gibt Zeiten, in denen die größte Stärke darin liegt, loszulassen. Alte Gewohnheiten, Menschen, Projekte oder Erwartungen. Nicht, weil sie schlecht waren, sondern weil jedes Loslassen Raum für etwas Neues schafft.

Mit 44 bin ich dankbarer denn je. Dankbar für die Menschen, die an mich glauben, mich inspirieren, mich fordern und meinen Weg begleiten. Aber auch für die Herausforderungen. Denn oft waren genau sie die größten Lehrmeister.

Heute weiß ich: Erfolg misst sich für mich nicht nur an Zahlen oder Titeln. Wahrer Erfolg bedeutet, die eigenen Werte zu leben, Menschen zu inspirieren und Spuren zu hinterlassen, die bleiben.

Ich starte voller Zuversicht in dieses neue Lebensjahr, mit neuen Visionen, klaren Zielen und dem festen Glauben daran, dass die größten Chancen oft dort entstehen, wo andere nur Unsicherheit sehen.

Denn das Leben wartet nicht auf den perfekten Moment. Es belohnt diejenigen, die den Mut haben, den ersten Schritt zu machen.

Von Herzen danke ich allen, die Teil meiner Reise sind. Danke für euer Vertrauen, eure Unterstützung und eure Wegbegleitung. ❤️

Auf 44. 😎

Auf neue Chancen.
Auf mutige Entscheidungen.
Auf persönliches Wachstum.

Und auf die Erkenntnis, dass jedes Ende gleichzeitig der Anfang von etwas Neuem sein kann.

Denn die schönsten Kapitel unseres Lebens entstehen nicht durch das, was hinter uns liegt, sondern durch den Mut, die nächste Seite aufzuschlagen.

Ich freue mich auf all…

📸 La photo du dimanche : Le Tour de France, 1986. © Sebastião Salgado / Courtesy Polka Galerie.

En 1986, le journal @liberationfr missionne @sebastiaosalgadooficial pour couvrir le Tour de France, aux côtés des cyclistes mais aussi des spectateurs, ce qui lui permet de faire halte dans chacun des villages. Dans cette série, inhabituelle, le photographe ne délaisse pas pour autant son obsession pour l’Homme et son environnement. « J’aimais déjà la France. Après ce Tour, je l’ai aimée encore plus», confie Sebastião Salgado. C’est ainsi que du 4 au 27 juillet 1986, le photographe brésilien a suivi chaque étape.

Les images de Salgado peignent alors un portrait de la France et de ses habitants. Finalement Salgado s’est intéressé davantage à la « France du bord des routes » qu’aux champions du Tour.
